title: CUET Computer Science Test 9
subject: Computer Science / Informatics Practices
syllabus_source: CUET SYLLABUS/Computer Science - 308.pdf (NTA syllabus for CUET (UG) 2026, latest published)
past_paper_reference: Pattern benchmark only: CUET (UG) 2025 308 paper structure and formats (no questions copied)
instructions: Attempt all 15 questions of Section A.
Then attempt all 35 questions of EITHER Section B1 (Computer Science) OR Section B2 (Informatics Practices) — 50 questions in total.
Each correct answer earns 5 marks; each incorrect answer deducts 1 mark; unattempted questions earn 0.

sections.title: Section A — Database Concepts, SQL and Computer Networks (compulsory)

questions.question: A school network must connect to the Internet, which uses different protocols, and all traffic must pass through one entry and exit point. Which device serves this purpose?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Gateway
Why: NCERT describes a gateway as the node that connects a network to an outside network that may use different protocols; it is the entry and exit point.
Why not the others: (B) only boosts signals. (C) connects devices inside a LAN. (D) connects one computer.
Key point: In homes, the router usually acts as the gateway.

questions.sub_topic: Order of rows sorted on a date
questions.question:
Table EVENT has the rows (Fair, '2024-02-10'), (Quiz, '2023-11-05'), (Play, '2024-01-20') and (Sports, '2024-02-01') for (Name, EDate). Arrange the names in the order of the output of SELECT Name FROM EVENT ORDER BY EDate DESC;
(A) Fair
(B) Quiz
(C) Play
(D) Sports
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (D), (C), (B)
Why: DESC puts the latest date first: 2024-02-10 (Fair), 2024-02-01 (Sports), 2024-01-20 (Play), 2023-11-05 (Quiz).
Why not the others: (A) is ascending order. (B) puts Play before Sports. (C) puts Sports before Fair.
Key point: Dates in 'YYYY-MM-DD' form sort correctly.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about MySQL data types:
(A) CHAR(n) stores fixed-length text.
(B) VARCHAR(10) always uses 10 bytes, whatever the length of the value.
(C) A DATE value is written in the form 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
(D) An INT column can store the value 12.5 exactly.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A) and (C) only
Why: CHAR is fixed-length and padded with spaces (A); DATE values use 'YYYY-MM-DD' (C).
Why not the others: Statement (B) is false — VARCHAR uses only the space needed by the value. Statement (D) is false — INT stores whole numbers; 12.5 needs FLOAT or DECIMAL. Options (A), (B) and (D) include one or both.
Key point: Choosing the right type saves space and prevents errors.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used as an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 172.31.255.254
Given: IPv4 needs exactly four numbers, each from 0 to 255.
Step 1: (C) has four parts, all within 0–255
Common mistake: (A) has 256. (B) has three parts. (D) has five parts.
Key point: An IPv4 address is 32 bits (4 × 8 bits).

questions.question: Table A_CLUB lists the students in the art club and B_CLUB those in the science club. Which query lists students who are in the art club but NOT in the science club?
options: A) SELECT Name FROM A_CLUB UNION SELECT Name FROM B_CLUB;
B) SELECT Name FROM A_CLUB MINUS SELECT Name FROM B_CLUB;
C) SELECT Name FROM A_CLUB INTERSECT SELECT Name FROM B_CLUB;
D) SELECT Name FROM A_CLUB, B_CLUB;
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) SELECT Name FROM A_CLUB MINUS SELECT Name FROM B_CLUB;
Why: MINUS (set difference) returns rows from the first query that do not appear in the second.
Why not the others: (A) lists students of either club. (C) lists students of both. (D) is a Cartesian product.
Key point: Set operations need the same number of columns in both queries.

questions.question: Table STU has the columns House and Marks with rows (Red, 72), (Blue, 55), (Red, 48), (Green, 90), (Blue, 81), (Red, 66). What does SELECT House, COUNT(*) FROM STU WHERE Marks >= 60 GROUP BY House; show for Red?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 2
Given: WHERE keeps only marks of 60 or more.
Step 1: Red rows: 72, 48, 66 → 72 and 66 qualify
Step 2: COUNT for Red = 2
Common mistake: (B) ignores WHERE. (C) misses one row. (D) counts all rows.
Key point: Rows removed by WHERE never reach the groups.

questions.question:
Match each constraint (List-I) with the example it enforces (List-II):

List-I
(A) NOT NULL
(B) UNIQUE
(C) DEFAULT
(D) FOREIGN KEY

List-II
(I) Every ClassID in STUDENT must exist in CLASS
(II) City is set to 'Delhi' if no city is given
(III) No two students can have the same e-mail
(IV) Every student must have a name
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NOT NULL forbids missing values (IV); UNIQUE forbids repeats (III); DEFAULT fills a value when none is given (II); FOREIGN KEY makes values refer to an existing primary key (I).
Why not the others: (B) swaps NOT NULL and UNIQUE; (C) swaps UNIQUE and DEFAULT; (D) swaps DEFAULT and FOREIGN KEY.
Key point: PRIMARY KEY combines NOT NULL and UNIQUE.

questions.question: Relation EMP has these (Name, City, Age) tuples: (Asha, Pune, 25), (Ravi, Delhi, 19), (Neha, Pune, 31), (Om, Agra, 22), (Ira, Delhi, 18). How many tuples are in π City (σ Age > 20 (EMP))?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 2 — Pune and Agra
Given: σ is applied first, then π, and duplicate tuples are removed.
Step 1: Age > 20 → Asha (Pune), Neha (Pune), Om (Agra)
Step 2: π City → Pune, Agra (Pune appears once)
Common mistake: (A) keeps a duplicate tuple. (C) ignores the selection. (D) misses Agra.
Key point: The result of a relational operation is again a relation, so it has no duplicates.

questions.question: Which command removes the column Remarks from the table STUDENT?
options: B) ALTER TABLE STUDENT DROP Remarks;
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) ALTER TABLE STUDENT DROP Remarks;
Why: ALTER TABLE … DROP column changes the structure by removing that column and its data.
Why not the others: (A) DELETE removes rows. (C) DROP TABLE removes the whole table. (D) UPDATE changes values.
Key point: ALTER TABLE … ADD adds a column.

questions.question: Relation STUDENT has degree 5 and cardinality 40. Two new columns are added and 10 new students are inserted. What are the new degree and cardinality?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Degree 7, cardinality 50
Given: Columns change the degree; rows change the cardinality.
Step 1: Degree = 5 + 2 = 7
Step 2: Cardinality = 40 + 10 = 50
Common mistake: (A) ignores the new columns. (B) ignores the new rows. (D) mixes the two changes.
Key point: Degree = number of attributes; cardinality = number of tuples.

questions.question: Table PRODUCT has the rows (Pen, 10), (Book, 120), (Bag, 450), (Ink, 25) for (Item, Price). After UPDATE PRODUCT SET Price = Price + 5 WHERE Price < 100;, what is SELECT SUM(Price) FROM PRODUCT; ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 615
Given: Only rows with Price < 100 change: Pen and Ink.
Step 1: Pen 10 → 15; Ink 25 → 30
Step 2: SUM = 15 + 120 + 450 + 30 = 615
Common mistake: (A) ignores the update. (B) updates every row. (C) updates only one row.
Key point: WHERE decides which rows UPDATE changes.

questions.question: What is the output of SELECT MID('KOLKATA', 4, 3); ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) KAT
Given: K(1) O(2) L(3) K(4) A(5) T(6) A(7).
Step 1: Start at position 4 and take 3 characters → K, A, T
Common mistake: (B) starts at 3. (C) takes the last three. (D) takes the first three.
Key point: SUBSTRING() and SUBSTR() work the same way.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A switch uses the network more efficiently than a hub.
Reason (R): A hub is a networking device with several ports.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both statements are true. A switch is more efficient because it sends each packet only to the port of the destination device, while a hub broadcasts to all ports. That a hub has several ports is true but does not explain the switch's efficiency.
Why not the others: (A) The Reason does not explain the Assertion. (C) and (D) Both are true.
Key point: Both a hub and a switch have many ports; they differ in how they forward data.

questions.sub_topic: Equi-join with one unmatched row on each side
questions.question: Table EMP has 4 rows with DeptID values D1, D2, D2, D5. Table DEPT has 3 rows with DeptID values D1, D2, D3 (each unique). How many rows does SELECT * FROM EMP E, DEPT D WHERE E.DeptID = D.DeptID; return?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 3
Given: A row appears for each pair with equal DeptID.
Step 1: D1 → 1 employee; D2 → 2 employees → 3 matching pairs
Step 2: D5 (EMP) and D3 (DEPT) have no match
Common mistake: (A) is the Cartesian product. (B) assumes every employee matches. (D) counts distinct departments.
Key point: Unmatched rows are dropped in an equi-join.

questions.question: Who decides which users may access which data in a database and makes sure regular backups are taken?
options: A) The end user of the app
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) The database administrator
Why: The DBA manages the database: controlling access, maintaining security, monitoring performance and arranging backup and recovery.
Why not the others: (A) only uses the data. (B) designs web pages. (C) supplies hardware.
Key point: The DBA works with the DBMS software.

questions.question: Which method can detect a NEW virus that is not yet in the antivirus database?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Heuristic (behaviour-based) detection
Why: Heuristic detection looks for suspicious behaviour or code patterns, so it can flag malware that has no known signature yet.
Why not the others: (A) needs a known signature. (C) and (D) do not detect malware.
Key point: Antivirus programs often combine both methods.

questions.question:
Match each measure (List-I) with its type (List-II):

List-I
(A) Mean
(B) Median
(C) Range
(D) Standard deviation

List-II
(I) Measure of central tendency
(II) Measure of variability (spread)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(I), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(II)
Why: Mean and median describe the centre (I); range and standard deviation describe the spread (II).
Why not the others: (B) calls the median a spread measure. (C) swaps mean and standard deviation. (D) calls the range a central measure.
Key point: Mode is also a measure of central tendency.

questions.question:
Arrange the steps of selection sort (ascending):
(A) Find the smallest element in the unsorted part
(B) Swap it with the first element of the unsorted part
(C) Move the boundary of the sorted part one position to the right
(D) Repeat until n − 1 passes are complete
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B), (C), (D)
Why: Each pass finds the minimum (A), swaps it into place (B) and grows the sorted part (C); the passes repeat n − 1 times (D).
Why not the others: (B) swaps before finding the minimum. (C) moves the boundary before swapping. (D) moves the boundary first.
Key point: After pass i, the first i elements are in their final positions.

questions.topic: B1: Exception and File Handling in Python
questions.sub_topic: tell() after seek() from the current position
questions.question:
poem.txt is opened in 'rb' mode. What is printed?

f = open('poem.txt', 'rb')
f.read(4)
f.seek(2, 1)
print(f.tell())
f.close()
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 6
Given: seek(offset, 1) moves relative to the current position.
Step 1: After read(4), the position is 4
Step 2: seek(2, 1) moves 2 bytes forward → 6
Common mistake: (A) treats it as seek(2) from the start. (B) ignores the seek. (D) assumes it rewinds.
Key point: whence 0 = start, 1 = current, 2 = end.

questions.question: Table STU has the rows (Asha, F, 82), (Ravi, M, 74), (Neha, F, 65), (Om, M, 90) for (Name, Gender, Marks). How many rows are returned by SELECT Name FROM STU WHERE Marks > 70 AND NOT Gender = 'F'; ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 2
Given: NOT Gender = 'F' means the gender is not F.
Step 1: Marks > 70 → Asha, Ravi, Om
Step 2: Not female → Ravi, Om → 2 rows
Common mistake: (A) misses one. (C) ignores NOT. (D) ignores both conditions.
Key point: NOT has higher priority than AND.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Calling dequeue on an empty queue causes underflow.
Reason (R): In a queue, elements are removed from the front.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: Both statements are true. Underflow happens because there is no element to remove. Where elements are removed (the front) does not explain why an empty queue cannot be dequeued, so the Reason is not the explanation.
Why not the others: (A) The Reason does not explain the Assertion. (C) and (D) Both statements are true.
Key point: Check isEmpty() before dequeue.

questions.question: What is the median of 14, 9, 21, 6, 18, 11?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 12.5
Given: Six values — the median is the average of the two middle ones.
Step 1: Sorted: 6, 9, 11, 14, 18, 21
Step 2: Median = (11 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12.5
Common mistake: (A) and (B) take one middle value. (D) is the mean (79 ÷ 6).
Key point: Always sort before finding the median.

questions.question: Linear search looks for 42 in [23, 8, 15, 42, 4, 16]. How many comparisons are made?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 4
Given: Compare from the first element until a match is found.
Step 1: 23, 8, 15 do not match; 42 matches at index 3
Step 2: Comparisons = 3 + 1 = 4
Common mistake: (A) gives the index. (C) checks every element. (D) is the best case.
Key point: The number of comparisons is position + 1 (counting from 0).

questions.topic: B1: Exception and File Handling in Python
questions.sub_topic: Counting lines that start with a letter
questions.question:
poem.txt contains these five lines:

The sun
is bright
The sky
is blue
Trees sway

What is printed?

c = 0
for line in open('poem.txt'):
    if line.startswith('T'):
        c += 1
print(c)
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 3
Given: Iterating over a file object gives one line at a time.
Step 1: Lines starting with 'T': 'The sun', 'The sky', 'Trees sway'
Step 2: c = 3
Common mistake: (B) misses 'Trees'. (C) counts all lines. (D) counts a line starting with 'i'.
Key point: startswith() is case-sensitive.

questions.question: Secretly listening to a private phone call or reading private messages as they are sent, without permission, is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Eavesdropping
Why: NCERT defines eavesdropping as the unauthorised real-time interception of private communication, such as calls, messages or video conferences.
Why not the others: (D) is sending unwanted bulk messages. (B) is copying data for safety. (C) is fixing program errors.
Key point: Encryption protects against eavesdropping.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about hashing:
(A) A hash function maps a key to an index (slot) of the hash table.
(B) A collision occurs when two keys are mapped to the same slot.
(C) Hashing works only on a sorted list.
(D) The remainder method uses h(key) = key % (table size).
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: NCERT describes the hash function (A), collisions (B) and the remainder method (D).
Why not the others: Statement (C) is false — hashing places keys by computation; no sorting is needed. Options (B), (C) and (D) include it.
Key point: A perfect hash function causes no collisions.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about sorting an already sorted list:
(A) Insertion sort makes only n − 1 comparisons.
(B) Bubble sort with a 'swapped' flag stops after one pass.
(C) Selection sort makes fewer comparisons than it does on an unsorted list.
(D) In the worst case, all three sorts are O(n²).
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: Sorted input is the best case for insertion sort (A) and for flagged bubble sort (B). In the worst case, all three are O(n²) (D).
Why not the others: Statement (C) is false — selection sort always makes n(n − 1)/2 comparisons, whatever the order. Options (A), (C) and (D) include it.
Key point: Selection sort cannot take advantage of sorted data.

questions.question: Table ATTENDANCE(RollNo, ADate, Status) stores one row per student per day. Which is the most suitable primary key?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (RollNo, ADate)
Why: A student appears on many days, and a date appears for many students, but each (RollNo, ADate) pair occurs once. This combination is a composite primary key.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) repeat on their own. (D) has only a few values such as P and A.
Key point: Every attribute of a composite key is needed for uniqueness.

questions.topic: B1: Exception and File Handling in Python
options: C) The program stops with a traceback
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Error: Invalid age
Given: raise throws the exception with the given message; 'as e' names the exception object.
Step 1: The except clause catches it
Step 2: print shows "Error:" followed by the message
Common mistake: (A) prints the type, not the message. (B) leaves out "Error:". (C) The exception is handled.
Key point: The raise statement is used to signal invalid situations.

questions.question: A student uses population figures published in the Census of India for a project. This is:
options: A) Primary data, because it is about people
B) Unstructured data, because it is very large
C) Metadata, because it is official
D) Secondary data, because it was collected by someone else
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Secondary data, because it was collected by someone else
Why: Secondary data is data collected earlier by another person or organisation and reused; the Census is collected by the government.
Why not the others: (A) Primary data is collected by the user. (B) Census tables are structured. (C) Metadata describes data.
Key point: Secondary data saves time but must be checked for relevance.

questions.topic: B1: Exception and File Handling in Python
questions.question:
Match each statement (List-I) with the exception it raises (List-II):

List-I
(A) int('x')
(B) [1, 2][5]
(C) {'a': 1}['b']
(D) 'a' + 1

List-II
(I) TypeError
(II) KeyError
(III) IndexError
(IV) ValueError
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: int('x') has a wrong value (IV); index 5 is out of range (III); key 'b' does not exist (II); adding a string and a number mixes types (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps ValueError and IndexError; (B) swaps IndexError and KeyError; (C) swaps KeyError and TypeError.
Key point: Each built-in exception names the kind of problem.

questions.topic: B1: Exception and File Handling in Python
questions.question: Which of the following is usually stored as a BINARY file?
options: C) A CSV file of marks
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A photograph (.jpg)
Why: NCERT explains that images, audio and video are stored as binary files — sequences of bytes not meant to be read as text.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are text files made of readable characters.
Key point: Binary files are opened in 'rb' or 'wb' mode.

questions.topic: B1: Computer Networks and Data Communication
questions.question:
Match each medium (List-I) with a typical application (List-II):

List-I
(A) Satellite link
(B) Optical fibre
(C) Infrared
(D) Bluetooth

List-II
(I) Wireless earphones connected to a phone
(II) TV remote control
(III) Undersea Internet backbone cables
(IV) Direct-to-home (DTH) television
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Satellites deliver DTH TV over wide areas (IV); optical fibre forms high-capacity backbones, including undersea cables (III); infrared works in remotes (II); Bluetooth links personal devices (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps satellite and fibre; (C) swaps fibre and infrared; (D) swaps infrared and Bluetooth.
Key point: Each medium suits a particular range and data rate.

questions.topic: B1: Computer Networks and Data Communication
questions.question: In which unit is the bandwidth of a communication channel measured?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Hertz (Hz)
Why: Bandwidth is the range of frequencies a channel can carry, so it is measured in Hertz (kHz, MHz, GHz).
Why not the others: (B) measures data size. (C) measures length. (D) measures power.
Key point: The data transfer rate is measured in bits per second.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of comparisons binary search needs for a sorted list of 100 elements?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 7
Given: Each comparison halves the remaining elements: 100 → 50 → 25 → 12 → 6 → 3 → 1.
Step 1: After 6 comparisons at most 1 element remains
Step 2: A 7th comparison settles it → 7 (⌊log₂ 100⌋ + 1 = 6 + 1)
Common mistake: (A) is linear search's worst case. (B) is half the list. (C) uses log₁₀ thinking or overcounts.
Key point: Doubling the list size adds only one comparison.

questions.question: Table TRIP has a column Mode with the values Bus, Train, Bus, Car, Train, Bus. How many rows are returned by SELECT DISTINCT Mode FROM TRIP; ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 3
Given: DISTINCT removes repeated values.
Step 1: Bus, Train, Car → 3 rows
Common mistake: (B) keeps duplicates. (C) misses Car. (D) gives only the most common.
Key point: COUNT(DISTINCT Mode) would return 3 as a single value.

questions.question:
For a queue stored in a list q (front at index 0), match each function (List-I) with its body (List-II):

List-I
(A) enqueue(q, x)
(B) dequeue(q)
(C) isEmpty(q)
(D) size(q)

List-II
(I) return len(q)
(II) return len(q) == 0
(III) return q.pop(0)
(IV) q.append(x)
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: enqueue adds at the rear with append (IV); dequeue removes from the front with pop(0) (III); isEmpty tests length 0 (II); size returns the length (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps enqueue and dequeue; (B) swaps dequeue and isEmpty; (D) swaps isEmpty and size.
Key point: dequeue should check isEmpty() first.

questions.sub_topic: What firewalls can and cannot do
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) A firewall can be hardware, software or both.
(B) A firewall filters traffic according to security rules.
(C) A firewall removes viruses from infected files.
(D) A firewall makes antivirus software unnecessary.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A) and (B) only
Why: NCERT describes firewalls as hardware or software (A) that allow or block traffic based on rules (B).
Why not the others: Statement (C) is false — cleaning infected files is the job of antivirus software. Statement (D) is false — firewalls and antivirus protect against different threats, so both are needed. Options (A), (B) and (D) include one or both.
Key point: Firewalls guard the network boundary.

questions.topic: B1: Computer Networks and Data Communication
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about wired media:
(A) Coaxial cable is used for cable television.
(B) Twisted pair cable is the costliest wired medium.
(C) Optical fibre offers the highest bandwidth among wired media.
(D) Coaxial cable is completely immune to all interference.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A) and (C) only
Why: Coaxial cable carries cable TV signals (A), and optical fibre has the highest bandwidth (C).
Why not the others: Statement (B) is false — twisted pair is the cheapest. Statement (D) is false — coaxial shielding reduces interference but does not eliminate it; only fibre is immune. Options (A), (B) and (C) include one or both.
Key point: Fibre is costly but fast and interference-free.

questions.question: Table FEE has 20 rows, none with Class = 'XIV'. What is the output of SELECT COUNT(Fee), MAX(Fee) FROM FEE WHERE Class = 'XIV'; ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 0, NULL
Given: No row satisfies the WHERE condition.
Step 1: COUNT of no values = 0
Step 2: MAX of no values = NULL
Common mistake: (A) makes COUNT NULL. (B) makes MAX 0. (C) counts all rows.
Key point: COUNT never returns NULL.

questions.topic: B1: Computer Networks and Data Communication
questions.sub_topic: Radio waves and line of sight
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Radio waves can pass through walls.
Reason (R): Radio waves need a clear line of sight between the sender and the receiver.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Why: The Assertion is true — radio waves are omnidirectional and can penetrate walls, which is why FM radio works indoors. The Reason is false — it is microwaves and infrared that need line of sight; radio waves do not.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) need a true Reason. (D) The Assertion is true.
Key point: Radio waves are used for FM radio and mobile communication.

questions.sub_topic: Early stop on a sorted list
questions.question: Linear search is applied to the sorted list [5, 9, 14, 20, 27, 33] to look for 18. With an 'early stop' rule, after which element can the search stop?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 20
Why: In a sorted list, once an element greater than the key (20 > 18) is reached, the key cannot appear later, so the search can stop and report 'not found'.
Why not the others: (A) and (D) are smaller than 18, so the search must continue. (B) is the last element; stopping there wastes comparisons.
Key point: Binary search is still faster for large sorted lists.

questions.question: What is [9, 4, 7, 3, 8] after the FIRST pass of bubble sort (ascending)?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) [4, 7, 3, 8, 9]
Given: 9 is swapped with each smaller neighbour as it moves right.
Step 1: (9,4) swap → [4, 9, 7, 3, 8]; (9,7) swap → [4, 7, 9, 3, 8]
Step 2: (9,3) swap → [4, 7, 3, 9, 8]; (9,8) swap → [4, 7, 3, 8, 9]
Common mistake: (A) is closer to pass 2. (B) is sorted. (C) stops early.
Key point: The largest value reaches the end in pass 1.

questions.question:
What is printed by the following code?

q = []
for x in "PQRS":
    q.append(x)
q.pop(0)
q.append('T')
q.pop(0)
print(q)
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) ['R', 'S', 'T']
Given: append() enqueues at the rear; pop(0) dequeues from the front.
Step 1: [P, Q, R, S] → remove P → [Q, R, S]
Step 2: add T → [Q, R, S, T] → remove Q → [R, S, T]
Common mistake: (B) removes from the rear. (C) dequeues only once. (D) dequeues three times.
Key point: A string can be iterated character by character.

questions.sub_topic: Setting up and checking a table
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (D), (A), (B)
Why: Create the database (C), select it (D), create the table (A), and then check its structure (B).
Why not the others: (A) creates the table before selecting the database. (B) uses the database before creating it. (D) describes a table that does not exist yet.
Key point: SHOW TABLES; would list MEMBER after step (A).

questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

A student converts the infix expression

A + B * ( C − D ) / E

to postfix using a stack, scanning from left to right with these rules:
• An operand goes straight to the output.
• '(' is pushed onto the stack.
• For ')', operators are popped to the output until '(' is found; the '(' is then discarded.
• For an operator, operators of HIGHER OR EQUAL precedence already on top of the stack (stopping at '(') are popped to the output first; then the new operator is pushed.
• At the end, all remaining operators are popped to the output.
(* and / have higher precedence than + and −.)

Question: Which operator is pushed onto the stack first?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) +
Given: The scan goes from left to right.
Step 1: A is output; then '+' is met and the stack is empty → '+' is pushed
Common mistake: (A) and (B) come later. (C) is inside the brackets.
Key point: Operands never go onto the stack in infix-to-postfix conversion.

questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

A student converts the infix expression

A + B * ( C − D ) / E

to postfix using a stack, scanning from left to right with these rules:
• An operand goes straight to the output.
• '(' is pushed onto the stack.
• For ')', operators are popped to the output until '(' is found; the '(' is then discarded.
• For an operator, operators of HIGHER OR EQUAL precedence already on top of the stack (stopping at '(') are popped to the output first; then the new operator is pushed.
• At the end, all remaining operators are popped to the output.
(* and / have higher precedence than + and −.)

Question: What are the stack contents (bottom to top) immediately after '(' has been pushed?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) [+, *, (]
Given: Tokens so far: A, +, B, *, (.
Step 1: '+' pushed; B output
Step 2: '*' has higher precedence than '+' on top, so nothing is popped; '*' is pushed
Step 3: '(' is pushed → [+, *, (]
Common mistake: (A) puts '(' below '*'. (C) puts '+' above '*'. (D) puts '(' at the bottom.
Key point: A higher-precedence operator waits above a lower one.

questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

A student converts the infix expression

A + B * ( C − D ) / E

to postfix using a stack, scanning from left to right with these rules:
• An operand goes straight to the output.
• '(' is pushed onto the stack.
• For ')', operators are popped to the output until '(' is found; the '(' is then discarded.
• For an operator, operators of HIGHER OR EQUAL precedence already on top of the stack (stopping at '(') are popped to the output first; then the new operator is pushed.
• At the end, all remaining operators are popped to the output.
(* and / have higher precedence than + and −.)

Question: What is the output string just after ')' has been processed?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) A B C D −
Given: After '(', the tokens C, −, D are read: C and D are output and '−' is pushed above '('.
Step 1: Output so far: A B C D
Step 2: ')' pops '−' to the output and discards '(' → A B C D −
Step 3: The stack is now [+, *]
Common mistake: (B) forgets to pop '−'. (C) also pops '*', which stays on the stack. (D) changes the operand order.
Key point: Brackets are never written in the postfix output.

questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

A student converts the infix expression

A + B * ( C − D ) / E

to postfix using a stack, scanning from left to right with these rules:
• An operand goes straight to the output.
• '(' is pushed onto the stack.
• For ')', operators are popped to the output until '(' is found; the '(' is then discarded.
• For an operator, operators of HIGHER OR EQUAL precedence already on top of the stack (stopping at '(') are popped to the output first; then the new operator is pushed.
• At the end, all remaining operators are popped to the output.
(* and / have higher precedence than + and −.)

Question: What is the complete postfix expression?
options: A) A B C D − E / * +
B) A B + C D − * E /
C) A B C D − * E / +
D) A B C D E − * / +
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) A B C D − * E / +
Given: After ')': output A B C D −, stack [+, *].
Step 1: '/' arrives: '*' on top has equal precedence → pop '*' → output A B C D − *; push '/'
Step 2: E is output → A B C D − * E
Step 3: End: pop '/' then '+' → A B C D − * E / +
Common mistake: (A) does not pop '*' before pushing '/'. (B) applies + first. (D) misplaces E.
Key point: Equal precedence pops first because * and / are left-associative.

questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

A student converts the infix expression

A + B * ( C − D ) / E

to postfix using a stack, scanning from left to right with these rules:
• An operand goes straight to the output.
• '(' is pushed onto the stack.
• For ')', operators are popped to the output until '(' is found; the '(' is then discarded.
• For an operator, operators of HIGHER OR EQUAL precedence already on top of the stack (stopping at '(') are popped to the output first; then the new operator is pushed.
• At the end, all remaining operators are popped to the output.
(* and / have higher precedence than + and −.)

Question: What is the value of the expression for A = 2, B = 6, C = 5, D = 3 and E = 4?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 5
Given: A + B * (C − D) / E = 2 + 6 × (5 − 3) ÷ 4.
Step 1: C − D = 2; B × 2 = 12
Step 2: 12 ÷ 4 = 3
Step 3: 2 + 3 = 5
Common mistake: (A) forgets to add A. (C) adds A before dividing: (2 + 12) / 4 is not the expression. (D) ignores the division.
Key point: Evaluating the postfix form A B C D − * E / + gives the same 5.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(A) Frequency polygon
(B) Histogram
(C) Box plot
(D) Scatter plot

List-II
(I) Points showing pairs of values of two variables
(II) Box from Q1 to Q3 with whiskers and outliers
(III) Adjacent bars showing frequencies of intervals
(IV) Line joining the mid-points of the tops of histogram bars
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: A frequency polygon joins mid-points of histogram bars (IV); a histogram shows interval frequencies (III); a box plot shows the five-number summary (II); a scatter plot shows pairs of values (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the first two; (C) swaps histogram and box plot; (D) swaps box plot and scatter plot.
Key point: Several of these describe the distribution of one variable.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – I
questions.question: For d = pd.DataFrame({'N': ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D'], 'P': [55, 82, 91, 67], 'Q': [78, 64, 88, 92]}), what is d[(d['P'] > 60) & (d['Q'] > 70)]['N'].tolist()?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) ['C', 'D']
Given: & needs both conditions to be True.
Step 1: P > 60 → B, C, D
Step 2: Q > 70 → A, C, D
Step 3: Both → C, D
Common mistake: (A) uses only P. (B) uses only Q. (C) misses D (67 > 60 and 92 > 70).
Key point: Use | for OR.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – II
questions.question: For e = pd.DataFrame({'x': [2, 4], 'y': [6, 8]}), what is e.mean(axis=1).tolist()?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) [4.0, 6.0]
Given: axis=1 averages across each row.
Step 1: Row 0: (2 + 6) ÷ 2 = 4.0; row 1: (4 + 8) ÷ 2 = 6.0
Common mistake: (A) gives column means. (C) is the overall mean. (D) gives row sums.
Key point: The default axis=0 averages each column.

questions.question:
Match each software product (List-I) with its category (List-II):

List-I
(A) Linux
(B) Microsoft Windows
(C) LibreOffice
(D) Microsoft Office

List-II
(I) FOSS
(II) Proprietary
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Linux and LibreOffice are free and open source (I); Windows and Microsoft Office are proprietary (II).
Why not the others: (A) reverses Linux and Windows. (B) reverses LibreOffice and Office. (D) calls Windows FOSS.
Key point: Python and Firefox are also FOSS.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – I
questions.question:
What is printed by the following code?

import pandas as pd
for lab, col in pd.DataFrame({'a': [1, 2], 'b': [3, 4]}).items():
    print(lab, col.sum())
options: B) a 1 / b 3 (one pair per line)
C) a 3 / b 7 (one pair per line)
D) a 4 / b 6 (one pair per line)
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) a 3 / b 7 (one pair per line)
Given: items() gives each column's label and the column as a Series.
Step 1: a → 1 + 2 = 3
Step 2: b → 3 + 4 = 7
Common mistake: (A) sums rows. (B) prints the first values. (D) sums across rows.
Key point: iterrows() loops over rows instead.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – I
questions.sub_topic: Choosing the index column when reading a CSV
questions.question: A CSV file has the columns AdmNo, Name and Class. Which statement makes AdmNo the row labels of the DataFrame?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) pd.read_csv('s.csv', index_col='AdmNo')
Why: index_col names the column to use as the index.
Why not the others: (A) header gives the row number of the header. (C) sep sets the separator. (D) transposes the data.
Key point: df.set_index('AdmNo') does the same after reading.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The bars of a histogram touch each other.
Reason (R): Histograms are mainly used for categorical data such as names of products.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Why: The Assertion is true — histogram bars are adjacent because the intervals are continuous. The Reason is false — histograms show the distribution of NUMERICAL data; categorical data uses bar charts, which have gaps between bars.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) need a true Reason. (D) The Assertion is true.
Key point: Bar chart → categories; histogram → numeric intervals.

questions.question: Which is an example of good netiquette in an online class?
options: A) Typing every message in capital letters to be noticed
B) Sharing the class meeting link publicly online
C) Posting jokes about classmates in the class chat
D) Muting the mic when not speaking and being polite
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Muting the mic when not speaking and being polite
Why: Netiquette means being respectful and responsible online — not disturbing others, being polite and protecting privacy.
Why not the others: (A) reads as shouting. (B) can let strangers in. (C) can hurt others.
Key point: Treat others online as you would in person.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – II
questions.question:
What is printed by the following code?

import pandas as pd
p = pd.DataFrame({'S': ['A', 'B', 'A', 'B', 'A'], 'Q': [1, 1, 2, 2, 1], 'M': [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]})
pt = p.pivot_table(index='S', columns='Q', values='M', aggfunc='mean')
print(pt.loc['A', 1])
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 30.0
Given: For S = 'A' and Q = 1, the rows have M = 10 and 50.
Step 1: Mean = (10 + 50) ÷ 2 = 30.0
Common mistake: (B) and (D) take one row. (C) is the sum.
Key point: The default aggfunc of pivot_table() is mean.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – I
questions.sub_topic: Columns and shape from a list of lists
questions.question:
What is printed by the following code?

import pandas as pd
l = pd.DataFrame([[1, 'x', 3.5], [2, 'y', 4.0]], columns=['id', 'c', 'v'])
print(l.columns.tolist(), l.shape)
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) ['id', 'c', 'v'] (2, 3)
Given: Each inner list is one row; columns names the columns.
Step 1: 2 rows × 3 columns → (2, 3)
Common mistake: (B) ignores the columns argument. (C) swaps rows and columns. (D) treats the first row as the header.
Key point: Without columns, labels would be 0, 1, 2.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – I
questions.question: What is printed by print(pd.Series(7, index=['x', 'y', 'z']).tolist())?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) [7, 7, 7]
Given: A scalar value is repeated for every index label.
Step 1: Three labels → [7, 7, 7]
Common mistake: (A) stores it once. (B) lists the index. (D) has no basis.
Key point: The index argument is required with a scalar.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – I
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I
(A) Dimensions of a Series
(B) Dimensions of a DataFrame
(C) Size of a Series
(D) Size of a DataFrame

List-II
(I) Mutable — rows and columns can be added or deleted
(II) Immutable — the number of elements is fixed once created
(III) Two
(IV) One
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: NCERT compares the two: a Series is 1-D (IV) with immutable size (II); a DataFrame is 2-D (III) with mutable size (I). The values of both are mutable.
Why not the others: (A) swaps the dimensions; (B) swaps the size rules; (C) mixes dimensions and size.
Key point: Each column of a DataFrame is a Series.

questions.question: The computers of a school building are connected to share a printer and files. This network is a:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) LAN
Why: A LAN covers a small area such as a room, building or campus.
Why not the others: (A) covers a few metres. (C) covers a city. (D) covers countries.
Key point: LANs are usually fast and privately owned.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – II
questions.question:
What is printed by the following code?

import pandas as pd
g = pd.DataFrame({'City': ['P', 'D', 'P', 'D', 'M'], 'Temp': [30, 40, 34, 38, 29]})
print(g.groupby('City')['Temp'].mean()['P'])
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 32.0
Given: The mean is found separately for each city.
Step 1: City P → 30 and 34
Step 2: Mean = 64 ÷ 2 = 32.0
Common mistake: (A) takes the first value. (B) is the sum. (D) is the overall mean (171 ÷ 5).
Key point: groupby splits, applies and combines.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – II
questions.question:
Arrange the steps to store a DataFrame df in a MySQL table:
(A) Import pandas and the connector library (e.g. sqlalchemy and pymysql)
(B) Create a connection (engine) to the MySQL database
(C) Call df.to_sql('marks', con, if_exists='replace', index=False)
(D) Check the table in MySQL with SELECT * FROM marks;
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B), (C), (D)
Why: Libraries are imported (A), a connection is made (B), the DataFrame is written (C), and the table is checked (D).
Why not the others: (A) connects before importing. (B) writes before connecting. (C) checks before writing.
Key point: if_exists='append' adds rows to an existing table instead.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – II
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) isnull() returns True for each missing value.
(B) notnull() returns True for each value that is present.
(C) dropna() changes the original DataFrame by default.
(D) fillna(0) replaces each missing value with 0.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: isnull() and notnull() are opposites (A, B), and fillna(0) fills with 0 (D).
Why not the others: Statement (C) is false — dropna() returns a new DataFrame; the original changes only with inplace=True or reassignment. Options (A), (C) and (D) include it.
Key point: Assign the result back, e.g. df = df.dropna().

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about e-waste:
(A) E-waste contains only harmless plastic.
(B) Burning e-waste in the open releases toxic fumes.
(C) E-waste breaks down naturally within a few weeks.
(D) Authorised recyclers can recover valuable metals from e-waste.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (B) and (D) only
Why: Open burning releases harmful gases (B), and recyclers recover metals such as copper and gold (D).
Why not the others: Statement (A) is false — e-waste contains toxic substances such as lead and mercury. Statement (C) is false — e-waste is not biodegradable. Options (A), (B) and (C) include one or both.
Key point: Reduce, reuse and recycle electronic goods.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) A hyperlink can be text or an image.
(B) A hyperlink can link only to another web page, never to a file.
(C) Hyperlinks work only within the same website.
(D) The World Wide Web is a system of web pages connected by hyperlinks.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A) and (D) only
Why: Hyperlinks can be text or images (A), and they connect pages to form the WWW (D).
Why not the others: Statement (B) is false — links can point to files such as PDFs and images. Statement (C) is false — links can point to any website. Options (B), (C) and (D) include one or both.
Key point: Hyperlinks are created in HTML with the <a> tag.

questions.question: Which argument of plt.plot() makes the markers larger?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) markersize=10
Why: markersize (or ms) sets the size of the markers drawn at the data points.
Why not the others: (A) changes line thickness. (C) changes line style. (D) changes colour.
Key point: marker='o' chooses the marker shape.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – I
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Operations on Pandas Series and DataFrames are fast for large data.
Reason (R): Pandas is built on top of NumPy, which provides fast operations on arrays.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
B) Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
C) Assertion is true, but Reason is false
D) Assertion is false, but Reason is true
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Why: NCERT notes that Pandas is built on NumPy; its data is stored in NumPy arrays, so computations are vectorised and fast. The Reason explains the Assertion.
Why not the others: (B) The Reason explains the Assertion. (C) and (D) Both are true.
Key point: Matplotlib is used alongside them for plotting.

questions.question: Which chart shows outliers as separate points beyond its whiskers?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Box plot
Why: A box plot draws whiskers to the furthest values within 1.5 × IQR and marks values beyond them as individual outlier points.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) do not identify outliers.
Key point: plt.boxplot(data) draws a box plot.

questions.question: A user installs a small program in the browser that blocks pop-up advertisements. This is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) A browser add-on
Why: Add-ons (extensions) add features to a browser, such as ad blocking or password management.
Why not the others: (A) hosts websites. (C) is a website's name. (D) is a small text file stored by a site.
Key point: Install add-ons only from trusted sources.

questions.question: plt.xticks([0, 1, 2], ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar']) is used in a program. What does it do?
options: A) Draws three bars that are named Jan, Feb and Mar
B) Sets the chart title to the text 'Jan Feb Mar'
C) Changes the scale of the y-axis to run from 0 to 2
D) Puts the labels Jan, Feb, Mar at x positions 0, 1, 2
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Puts the labels Jan, Feb, Mar at x positions 0, 1, 2
Why: xticks(positions, labels) sets where ticks appear on the x-axis and what text is shown at each.
Why not the others: (A) needs bar(). (B) needs title(). (C) concerns the y-axis.
Key point: yticks() does the same for the y-axis.

questions.question:
Arrange the following phases of a project in the usual order:
(A) Test the solution
(B) Research and collect data
(C) Plan the project
(D) Present the outcome
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C), (B), (A), (D)
Why: The team first plans (C), then researches and gathers data (B), builds and tests the solution (A), and finally presents it (D).
Why not the others: (A) researches before planning. (B) tests before research. (D) presents before testing.
Key point: Each phase depends on the one before it.

questions.sub_topic: Plotting a DataFrame as a bar chart
questions.question:
For df with the columns Name and Marks, consider df.plot(kind='bar', x='Name', y='Marks'):
(A) x='Name' puts the names on the x-axis.
(B) y='Marks' uses the Marks values as bar heights.
(C) Changing kind to 'barh' draws horizontal bars.
(D) plot() cannot be used on a DataFrame; it works only on a Series.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: x and y choose the columns (A, B), and kind='barh' gives horizontal bars (C).
Why not the others: Statement (D) is false — plot() is available for both DataFrames and Series. Options (B), (C) and (D) include it.
Key point: Pandas plotting uses Matplotlib, so plt.show() displays it.

questions.question: Why should the operating system and apps be kept updated?
options: A) They often fix security weaknesses attackers could use
B) They delete all the personal files stored on the device
C) They switch off the antivirus to save memory
D) They make the use of passwords unnecessary
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) They often fix security weaknesses attackers could use
Why: NCERT includes updating software in cyber safety measures, because updates patch known security holes.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are false.
Key point: Turn on automatic updates where possible.

questions.question: Software released under the GNU General Public License (GPL) is modified by a developer who wants to distribute the new version. What does the GPL require?
options: A) The new version must be sold for a price
B) It must also be released under the GPL with source
C) The original author's name must be removed from it
D) The new version must be kept secret from all users
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) It must also be released under the GPL with source
Why: The GPL is a copyleft licence: modified versions that are distributed must carry the same freedoms — released under the GPL with source code available.
Why not the others: (A) Selling is allowed but not required. (C) Credit must be kept. (D) contradicts distribution.
Key point: Linux is released under the GPL.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – II
questions.question: For r = pd.DataFrame({'N': ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'], 'M': [50, 90, 70, 85]}), what is r.sort_values('M', ascending=False).head(2)['N'].tolist()?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) ['b', 'd']
Given: Descending sort, then the first two rows.
Step 1: Order: b (90), d (85), c (70), a (50)
Step 2: Top two: b, d
Common mistake: (A) sorts ascending. (B) skips d. (C) reverses the top two.
Key point: nlargest(2, 'M') gives the same rows.

questions.question:
Match each top-level domain (List-I) with the kind of website it usually indicates (List-II):

List-I
(A) .edu
(B) .gov
(C) .org
(D) .in

List-II
(I) A website registered in India
(II) A non-profit organisation
(III) A government body
(IV) An educational institution
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: .edu indicates education (IV); .gov government (III); .org non-profit organisations (II); .in is India's country-code domain (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps .edu and .gov; (B) swaps .gov and .org; (C) swaps .org and .in.
Key point: Domain names are read from right to left.

questions.topic: B2: Data Handling using Pandas – I
questions.question: For s = pd.Series([5, 15, 25, 35]), what is (s + 10)[s > 10].tolist()?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) [25, 35, 45]
Given: s + 10 adds 10 to every value; the mask s > 10 is computed on the original s.
Step 1: s + 10 = [15, 25, 35, 45]
Step 2: s > 10 → [False, True, True, True]
Step 3: Result = [25, 35, 45]
Common mistake: (A) ignores the mask. (C) applies the mask to s, not s + 10. (D) uses the mask (s + 10) > 30.
Key point: The mask and the Series must have the same index.

questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Table ORDERS of an online shop:

OID | Customer | ODate | Amount
101 | Ravi | 2024-01-15 | 1200
102 | Sana | 2024-03-08 | 800
103 | Ravi | 2024-03-22 | 1500
104 | Tom | 2023-12-30 | 600
105 | Sana | 2024-07-04 | 950

Question: What is the output of SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS WHERE YEAR(ODate) = 2024; ?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) 4
Given: YEAR() extracts the year.
Step 1: 2024 dates: 101, 102, 103, 105 → 4
Step 2: 104 is in 2023
Common mistake: (B) ignores the condition. (C) misses one order. (D) counts the 2023 order.
Key point: YEAR(), MONTH() and DAY() return numbers.

Question: What is the output of SELECT MONTHNAME(ODate) FROM ORDERS WHERE OID = 102; ?
questions.explanation:

Given: Order 102 has ODate '2024-03-08'.
Step 1: Month 03 → March
Common mistake: (A) is MONTH(). (B) is order 101's month. (D) is a day name.
Key point: DAYNAME() would give the weekday instead.

Step 2: SUM = 2300

Question: What is the output of the following query? (4 July 2024 was a Thursday.)

SELECT DAYNAME(MAX(ODate)) FROM ORDERS WHERE Customer = 'Sana';
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Thursday
Given: Sana's orders: '2024-03-08' and '2024-07-04'.
Step 1: MAX(ODate) = '2024-07-04' (the latest)
Step 2: DAYNAME('2024-07-04') = Thursday
Common mistake: (A) uses the earlier order (8 March 2024 was a Friday). (C) is MONTHNAME(). (D) skips DAYNAME().
Key point: An aggregate's result can be passed to another function.

Question: What is the FIRST value in the output of SELECT OID FROM ORDERS ORDER BY ODate; ?
questions.explanation:

Given: ORDER BY sorts dates from earliest to latest by default.
Step 1: The earliest date is 2023-12-30 → order 104
Common mistake: (B) is the first row as stored. (C) is the latest. (D) has no basis.
Key point: Add DESC for latest first.
